subject: Dedicated cluster baseline + scale-trigger blueprint for HelixWorks
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Rinaldi <marta@helixworks.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-05T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated cluster baseline + scale-trigger blueprint for HelixWorks

Hi Marta — great to meet yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a first-pass blueprint for a dedicated cluster that matches the production traffic profile you shared (90th p95 latency target, mixed chat + embeddings workload). Key highlights (attached PDF + cost workbook):

- Baseline: 24 A100-equivalent GPUs (min guaranteed) to cover steady-state peak during business hours (expected sustained throughput ~1.2M tokens/min across 60 concurrent sessions).
- Burst: Auto-burst pool up to 72 GPUs for predictable daytime spikes (billing on usage).
- Ramp plan: 3-month staged onramp — Week 0: 24 GPUs live (canary), Week 4: +12 GPUs (36 total), Week 8: +12 GPUs (48 total), option to unlock burst to 72 at Week 12 if metrics validated.
- Scale-trigger rules (recommended): autoscale step when 95th pct queue latency > 120ms for 10 minutes or token-drop rate > 3% for 5 minutes. Slowdown fallback to a cheaper, quantized model variant when burst capacity unavailable.
- SLAs: aiming for 99.9% service availability for the baseline lane; higher-tier SLA optional for dedicated lanes with extended credits.

Questions for you before I iterate: are there hard budget caps for month 1 vs month 3? Any SOC2/contract redlines your procurement team requires up front? I’ve copied Vanessa (onboarding/ops) and Ben (pricing) to keep this tight.

Thanks — I’ll hold a short review call if you want to walk through the workbook.

—Sean Gallagher
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: helixworks_capacity_blueprint_v1.pdf, cost_model_v2.xlsx

From: Marta Rinaldi <marta@helixworks.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@helixworks.ai>, Procurement <procurement@helixworks.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster baseline + scale-trigger blueprint for HelixWorks

Thanks Sean — this looks like the right level of detail. A few clarifications before we move to procurement:

1) Baseline vs min guarantee: does the 24 GPU "baseline" mean we are contractually committing to 24 GPUs (monthly minimum)? We want a firm minimum for capacity planning but flexibility to grow.
2) Can you break down the cost delta between 24 -> 36 and 36 -> 48 in the workbook by token unit and by latency bucket?
3) We will need a 7-day canary window on each activation step and a rollback playbook.
4) Security: procurement asked whether logs and audit retention can be kept in our VPC for the Dedicated control plane.

Also looping Ethan (CTO) for the technical acceptance criteria — Ethan, any immediate red flags on the throughput numbers?

Best,
Marta Rinaldi
Head of Product, HelixWorks
marta@helixworks.ai

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Rinaldi <marta@helixworks.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-06T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster baseline + scale-trigger blueprint for HelixWorks

Hi Marta — quick operational notes from onboarding/ops side:

- The 24-GPU minimum would be configured as a reserved lane with dedicated GPU pool and warm instances; we treat that as the "min guaranteed" for scheduling and pre-warming. That matches your ask for firm minimums.
- Canary windows: we recommend a 7-day canary for the initial 24 -> 36 activation, with 3-day smoke checks after incremental 12-GPU additions thereafter. We can add automated canary health checks (p95 latency, error rate, cold-starts) to the rollout job.
- VPC & logs: Dedicated supports sending audit logs and Control Plane events to customer-managed logging (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/S3) and KMS for key control. We'll include the retention and export details in the SOC2 appendix.

Operational acceptance checklist (short):
- Baseline traffic ingestion validated on staging (we'll replay a 72-hour traffic window).
- Canary monitoring configured in Console with alerting to HelixWorks on-call.
- Rollback policy: automatic rollback if p95 latency degrades >25% for 15 consecutive minutes or error rate >5% for 5 minutes.

I attached a short onboarding-runbook snippet to the Drive link. Happy to run a joint runbook session next week.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Rinaldi <marta@helixworks.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-08T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing & min-GPU structuring options

Marta — thanks for the detailed review. Two pricing structures that map to your ramp:

Option A (Commit-min): 24 GPU guaranteed monthly commit at a blended rate; burst billed at on-demand rates. Month 1: invoice for 24 GPUs. Month 2/3: invoice adjusted per actual committed increase (if you opt into +12 or +24). This gives predictable invoices for finance.

Option B (Flex-tranche): Minimum 12-GPU tranche x2 with a step-up commitment fee that unlocks the next tranche. Lower upfront OPEX, higher per-GPU marginal cost during burst.

In both options we can include an activation credit (one-time) to offset canary validation costs and a two-week SLA credit holdback applied if initial baseline SLAs miss target. I updated cost_model_v2.xlsx with per-token cost buckets and a projection table for the 3-month ramp.

If procurement needs, we can convert to a monthly minimum-dollar commitment vs. GPU count. Thoughts? If you confirm Option A or B I’ll prepare the pricing appendix and a draft SOW for legal.

—Ben Carter
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@helixworks.ai>
To: Procurement <procurement@helixworks.ai>, Marta Rinaldi <marta@helixworks.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-10T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster baseline + scale-trigger blueprint for HelixWorks

Thanks everyone — we reviewed the workbook and ops notes. We’re aligned with Option A (24 GPU minimum commit) with the staged activations at Weeks 4 and 8. Procurement: please note we require a 30-day termination notice after Month 6 and an audit clause to validate logs retention in our VPC.

Action items before SOW:
- Sean / Ben: update pricing appendix to show month-by-month invoice samples under Option A and include the activation credit line.
- Vanessa: include the canary runbook and rollback playbook in the onboarding appendix.
- Legal/procurement: will share a redline set next week; please add the SOC2 appendix per our security checklist.

If those are doable we’ll instruct finance to approve the PO and start the DocuSign flow.

—Ethan Cole
CTO, HelixWorks
ethan.cole@helixworks.ai
